as_told.title: Buffalo Soldiers as Freemasons and the 'as above, so below' inscription

plain: On Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, someone carved the old saying "as above, so below" into the rock, and Michels says nobody knows who made it or why. He suggests it might be the work of Augustus Walley, a legendary buffalo soldier (one of the Black US Army soldiers of the late 1800s) who was given the Medal of Honor. In a later episode he leaves Walley's name out, points to the inscription again and asks whether it is a coincidence that the buffalo soldiers were Freemasons, members of a brotherhood known for its secret symbols.
